label: What you need
q: Could you tell me a bit more about what you need?
ex: For example: "an agency to run a client dinner for 40 people in March".

label: Category (Level 4)
q: Which of these categories fits your request best?

label: Budget
why: The amount decides how much competition is needed.

label: What it is for
q: What is it for?
ex: For example: "a farewell gift for a colleague" or "our team offsite in March".

label: Start / delivery
ex: A date or "as soon as possible" is fine.

label: Why this supplier
ex: For example: they built the current system, or nobody else offers it.
why: Without a reason, a purchase this size needs competing offers.

label: Data and system access
q: Will the provider see or access any of our or our clients' data, systems, money or accounts? If so, which, and with what access?

label: Technology involved
q: Will the provider supply or run any technology for this, for example software, a system they host, IT support or data feeds?

label: Runs it for us
q: Will the provider run something for us on an ongoing basis that we would otherwise do ourselves?

label: Acceptance and sign-off
q: How will the work be checked and accepted, and who signs it off?

label: Support and tools
q: How will the technology be supported: support model, service hours and tools?

label: Supplier standard terms
ex: Online terms can change without notice, so they need a fixed copy.

label: Provisioning legal entity
q: Which legal entity of the bank will receive this service and sign the contract?
ex: It goes on the contract and into the register of third-party arrangements.

label: Work the bank could do itself
q: Is this work the bank does itself today, or could realistically do itself?
ex: This is the key question for whether it counts as outsourcing: it can apply even if we have never done it ourselves, as long as a bank could realistically do it.

label: Dependencies and assumptions
q: What will we need to provide, and what is the provider assuming?

label: Checked by you
q: Please check what I've worked out.

label: Budget approved
q: Is the budget already approved?
why: Sourcing only starts once the budget is confirmed.

label: Role
q: What role do you need to fill?
ex: For example: "senior Java developer" or "interim project manager".

label: People
q: How many people?

label: Key skills
q: What skills or experience must they have?
ex: For example: "Java 17, Spring Boot, payments experience".

label: Rate or budget
q: Do you have a day rate or total budget in mind?
ex: For example: "around €700 a day" or "€150k in total". "Not sure" is fine.

label: System access
q: Will they need access to our systems or client data?

label: Changes
q: Does anything change compared with the current contract?
ex: For example: "same scope, 20% more volume" or "no changes".

label: Use existing contract
ex: That's usually the quickest way, because no new competition is needed.

label: Problem to solve
q: What business problem does this solve? And what happens if it's delayed?

label: Target audience
q: Who is the primary audience: who will use it or benefit from it?

label: Supported functions
q: Which functions or teams of the organisation does it support?

label: Key benefits
q: What are the main benefits and measurable outcomes?

label: Unique selling points
q: What makes it different from what you have today, or from other options?

label: Regulatory / governance benefits
q: Does it bring regulatory, control, governance or resilience benefits?

label: Service profile
q: Here's how I'd describe the rest of the service. Does this fit, or what would you change?

label: If it doesn't go ahead
q: What happens if this doesn't go ahead, or is delayed?
ex: Think of operations, regulators, clients or cost. For example: "we miss the audit deadline" or "manual work continues, nothing serious".

label: Acceptance criteria
q: How will you know the work has been done well?

label: Most important
q: When we compare offers, what matters most to you?

label: Supplier must have
q: Must the supplier have any certifications or specific experience?

label: Today's provider
q: Is this replacing or continuing something you have today?
ex: If so, who provides it now? "No, it's new" is fine.

label: Install & support
q: Do you need installation, warranty or ongoing support with it?
ex: For example: on-site installation and a 3-year warranty.

label: Data involved
q: What kind of data will they see, and where would it be stored?
ex: For example: "employee names and salaries, stored in the EU".
why: This shapes the data protection review.

label: If it stopped
q: If this stopped working for a day, what would happen?
ex: For example: "clients couldn't log in" or "a short delay, nothing serious".
why: It tells us how critical the supplier is.

label: Subcontractors
q: Is the supplier likely to use subcontractors or teams in other countries?

label: Payment model
q: How would you prefer to pay?
ex: A fixed price suits a clear scope, a day rate suits flexible work, and a monthly fee suits an ongoing service.

label: Service levels
q: Which service levels matter to you?

label: Who owns the work
q: Should we own what the supplier creates, such as designs, code or materials?

label: Supplier so far
ex: Anything to fix in the renewal is useful to know.

label: Who runs it
q: Who will host and run the software: the provider (SaaS or a managed service), or our own Technology team?
ex: This decides the outsourcing check: software the provider runs for us usually counts as outsourcing, software we install and run ourselves does not.

label: Phasing
q: Should any part be delivered first?
ex: For example: "the KYC part first, trading in a second release".
